name: Dynamic Table Schema Projection Runtime Integration
description: Connect bun-graph-db runtime table schema projections to table-scoped MCP input schemas, create/update node validation, schema-change invalidation, documentation, and final GraphQL/MCP smoke verification. This plan assumes the current projection core, repository service, and SchemaMapper adapter already exist and focuses on completing the path to runtime use.

userStories.title: Establish bun-graph-db baseline runtime health
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a current baseline of install, focused tests, typecheck, lint, build, and smoke status so that projection integration failures can be separated from pre-existing runtime issues.
acceptanceCriteria: Run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` from `references/bun-graph-db` and document whether dependencies are already current or changed.
Run focused projection tests: `bun test tests/unit/schema/table-schema-projection.test.ts tests/unit/schema/table-schema-projection-service.test.ts`.
Run `bun run typecheck` and record pass/fail.
Run `bun run lint --max-diagnostics=20` and record pass/fail.
Run `bun run build` and record pass/fail.
Run a basic GraphQL health smoke using an isolated server helper or a background server that is stopped cleanly.
Run a table-scoped MCP smoke if a reliable helper already exists; otherwise document the missing helper as a follow-up for the final integration story.
Do not change runtime behavior in this story except for minimal test harness fixes required to establish baseline.
Focused projection tests pass.
bun run typecheck passes, or failures are documented as pre-existing and unrelated.
bun run lint --max-diagnostics=20 passes, or failures are documented as pre-existing and unrelated.
userStories.notes: PRD review improvement: preflight must run first so ralph does not confuse existing bun-graph-db health issues with projection integration regressions.

userStories.title: Wire projection service into table-scoped MCP tools/list
userStories.description: As an MCP client, I want table-scoped tools/list to expose projection-derived input schemas so that the current dynamic table attributes are visible to AI tools.
acceptanceCriteria: `TableMcpServer` can construct or receive `TableSchemaProjectionService` without creating hard coupling from core schema code to repositories.
Create/update node table-scoped tools use `SchemaMapper.mapTableProjectionToMcpInputSchema(projection)` for their input schemas where applicable.
Existing table-scoped tools remain listed.
`tools/list` for a table includes an `attributes` object with the current table attributes.
Required attributes appear in `attributes.required`.
Projection diagnostics are surfaced safely as metadata or warnings without crashing tools/list unless the table projection is unusable.
A focused test verifies tools/list output includes projection-derived attributes.
Focused projection tests pass.
bun run typecheck passes, or failures are documented as pre-existing and unrelated.
bun run lint --max-diagnostics=20 passes, or failures are documented as pre-existing and unrelated.
userStories.notes: PRD review improvement: skip reimplementing core projection/service; consume the existing `TableSchemaProjectionService` and `SchemaMapper` adapter.

userStories.title: Validate createNode attributes with table projection
userStories.description: As a data user, I want createNode attribute payloads validated against the current table projection so that invalid dynamic table data is rejected consistently.
acceptanceCriteria: Identify the createNode execution path used by GraphQL, REST, and table-scoped MCP flows.
CreateNode validation obtains the current projection by `tableId` before persisting attribute values.
Missing required attributes produce structured validation errors.
Unknown attributes produce structured validation errors.
Enum violations produce structured validation errors.
Numeric constraint violations produce structured validation errors.
Existing valid createNode flows still pass.
Focused tests cover valid create input, missing required attribute, unknown attribute, enum violation, and numeric constraint violation.
Focused projection tests pass.

bun run lint --max-diagnostics=20 passes, or failures are documented as pre-existing and unrelated.
userStories.notes: Keep validation logic projection-based; do not add a separate hand-written validator for createNode.

userStories.title: Validate updateNode attributes with partial projection rules
userStories.description: As a data user, I want updateNode attribute payloads validated against the current table projection while allowing valid partial updates.
acceptanceCriteria: Identify the updateNode execution path used by GraphQL, REST, and table-scoped MCP flows.
UpdateNode validation obtains the current projection from the existing node table or request table context.
Partial updates do not require all required attributes when only changing existing node fields.
Unknown updated attributes produce structured validation errors.
Enum violations produce structured validation errors.
Numeric constraint violations produce structured validation errors.
Table mismatch is rejected when update input includes a conflicting table context.
Existing valid update flows still pass.
Focused tests cover valid partial update, unknown attribute, enum violation, numeric constraint violation, and table mismatch where applicable.
Focused projection tests pass.
bun run typecheck passes, or failures are documented as pre-existing and unrelated.
bun run lint --max-diagnostics=20 passes, or failures are documented as pre-existing and unrelated.
userStories.notes: This is separate from createNode because partial-update required-field semantics are different and should not be conflated.

userStories.title: Invalidate table-scoped MCP schema cache on schema changes
userStories.description: As an MCP user, I want table-scoped MCP tools to refresh after table schema changes so that stale input schemas do not remain cached.
acceptanceCriteria: Attribute create flow triggers table schema invalidation.
Attribute update flow triggers table schema invalidation.
Attribute delete flow triggers table schema invalidation if such a flow exists; otherwise document the missing flow.
AttributeType update/delete triggers invalidation for affected tables.
Table delete removes or invalidates the table-scoped MCP server cache.
`TableMcpServerFactory.refreshServerForTable(tableId)` or an equivalent invalidation boundary is used instead of rebuilding all table servers.
Unchanged tables keep existing cache behavior.
Focused tests verify cached table MCP schema changes after an attribute schema change.
Focused projection tests pass.

userStories.notes: PRD review improvement: invalidation should be table-scoped, not global, to preserve dynamic table performance.

userStories.title: Invalidate generated templates and table docs on schema changes

Existing docs generation behavior remains backward compatible.
`TableTemplateAutoGenerator` no longer relies on misleading `dataType: 'string'` fallback when attribute type data is available.
Tests verify table docs/schema metadata changes after attribute type changes.
Tests verify generated template metadata is refreshed or marked stale after table schema changes.

The document lists what is explicitly not shared yet.
The document defines criteria for when to extract a shared package or module.
